title: A TRPO step: Fisher-vector product and line search
goal:
Put the pieces of Section 6 and Appendix C together on a softmax policy.

The policy picks one of $K$ actions in each of $N$ sampled states, with logits $\phi(s, a)^\top \theta$. The array `phi` has shape `(N, K, d)` and `theta` has shape `(d,)`. The starter includes `probs` and a finished `conjugate_gradient` (your solution from Exercise 3). Write two functions:

- `fisher_vector_product(phi, theta, v)` returns $Fv$ for the Fisher matrix $F$, which is the Hessian of the mean KL divergence at `theta` (Appendix C.1). Never build the $d \times d$ matrix. For each state, center the features, $c_k = \phi_k - \sum_j p_j \phi_j$. Then $Fv$ is the average over states of $\sum_k p_k\, c_k\,(c_k \cdot v)$.
- `trpo_step(theta_old, g, fvp, delta, surrogate, kl, shrink=0.5, max_backtracks=10)` returns the new parameters. Compute $s \approx F^{-1} g$ with 10 CG iterations, then $\beta = \sqrt{2\delta / s^\top F s}$. Then run the line search from Appendix C: try $\theta_{old} + \text{shrink}^k \beta s$ for $k = 0, 1, \dots$, and return the first candidate with `kl(theta) <= delta` and `surrogate(theta) > surrogate(theta_old)`. If none qualifies, return `theta_old`.

The tests check `fisher_vector_product` against a finite-difference Hessian of the KL, and they check the line search with objectives where the quadratic model is wrong.
hints: `p = probs(phi, theta)` has shape `(N, K)`. `phi_bar = np.einsum("nk,nkd->nd", p, phi)` is the mean feature per state.
`c @ v` has shape `(N, K)`: the dot product of every centered feature with `v`. Then `np.einsum("nk,nkd,nk->d", p, c, c @ v)` sums $p_k c_k (c_k \cdot v)$ over actions and states. Divide by `N`.
Without centering, you get the second moment of the features instead of their covariance under the policy. The result looks reasonable and is wrong.
In the line search, test both conditions. The step $\beta s$ uses a quadratic model of the KL and a linear model of the objective, so either can fail for the real functions.
